scenes.text: Imagine standing in a breathtaking, silent forest deep inside Yellowstone National Park where you suddenly realize that the laws of the land literally do not apply to you.
Because of a bizarre, overlooked loophole in the United States Constitution, you could theoretically commit a serious crime in this fifty-square-mile zone and legally walk away completely free.
This is because this specific strip of land sits in Idaho but the park is managed by Wyoming, meaning a local jury is constitutionally required but absolutely nobody lives there to form one.
This creates a terrifying, real-life legal black hole that politicians still haven't fixed, so would you ever dare to visit this place, or will you follow for more crazy secrets?
